content.title: Becoming a Productive Muslim
content.subtitle: Key Lessons from the Webinar
content.body:
🎥 Missed the webinar or want to watch it again?

Watch the full Facebook Live recording: https://web.facebook.com/share/v/1JoiEzzBwR/

Alhamdulillah! In the recent Ansar Special Webinar – "Productive Muslim: Why, What and How?", our respected guest Shahriar Khan (Certified Productive Muslim Trainer) shared that productivity is not only about time management or getting more work done. It is about building a conscious, balanced, and barakah-filled life as a Muslim. Here are a few key lessons from the session.

"Bismillah"—Not Just a Word, but a Mindset

We say "Bismillah" before almost every task. But how often do we truly feel, "I am beginning in Allah's name. He will help me and place barakah in this work."

When this belief settles in the heart, even an ordinary task becomes an act of worship. A productive Muslim's greatest strength is not planning, but complete tawakkul in Allah.

Version 1.0 → Version 1.1

One of our biggest mistakes is expecting instant change. We want to become a different person overnight. Today we are irregular in salah, and tomorrow we expect ourselves to pray Tahajjud, recite the Qur'an daily, make lengthy dhikr, and do everything at once.

Such change rarely lasts. As explained in the webinar, if you are Version 1.0 today, your goal tomorrow is not Version 10.0, but Version 1.1. One salah on time today is Version 1.1. Tomorrow, perhaps you will pray it in congregation. Then, step by step, your Qur'an, dhikr, Tahajjud, family life, and character will improve. Every small step moves you forward.

Productivity Means a Balanced Life

Being busy is not productivity. If work makes us neglect salah, family, health, or spiritual growth, there is no barakah in that achievement. True productivity is maintaining balance between the rights of Allah, yourself, your family, and society.

A Special Update for Ansar Members
